case_title: Chhannu Lal Verma v. The State of Chhattisgarh
aggravating_circumstances: Murder of three persons, premeditated, cruelty, grievous injuries to three persons, two deceased and one injured were women
mitigating_circumstances: Previously acquitted in Section 376, IPC, good behavior in prison
neutral_facts: The accused entered the house of the victim and caused fatal injuries to three individuals with a knife. He then went to another house and assaulted another individual, causing grievous injuries. The accused was convicted of murder, attempt to murder, threatening to kill, and house trespass. The trial court sentenced him to life imprisonment and death penalty, considering the brutality of the crime and the premeditated nature of the act. The High Court confirmed the conviction and death sentence, citing aggravating circumstances such as the murder of three persons and the infliction of grievous injuries. The accused had a previous criminal record involving a rape charge that was later acquitted. The Supreme Court commuted the death sentence to life imprisonment, emphasizing the need to consider the possibility of reform and rehabilitation, as well as the failure of the High Court to properly apply the 'rarest of rare' test.
